class.name: PlayerTouchButton
class.brief_description: On-screen button that holds an action on one player's own [PlayerInput].
class.description: [b]Godot's [TouchScreenButton] covers the single-player case and covers it well.[/b] This differs in two ways: it writes to a [PlayerInput] rather than to the global [Input] singleton, so with two people on one machine it acts for one of them; and it is a [Control], so it anchors alongside the rest of the HUD instead of sitting in world space as a [Node2D]. It tracks its finger by index for the same reason [PlayerVirtualJoystick] does, and never marks events handled. Hiding the node releases the action, so a button hidden while held cannot leave it stuck down.

method.name: is_pressed
method.description: Whether a finger is currently on the button.

method.name: reset
method.description: Drops the finger and releases the action. Hiding the node does this for you.

members.member: The action held for as long as a finger is on the button.
Draws a plain filled outline in the chosen [member shape]. Ignored when [member texture_normal] is set; turn it off to draw the button yourself.
Which [LocalPlayer] this button belongs to. With no local player yet, it writes to the global [Input] singleton instead.
The hit area, tested against this control rect.
Drawn stretched over the control rect instead of the default shape.

signal.name: pressed
signal.description: A finger landed on the button.

signal.name: released
signal.description: The finger lifted, or the button was reset or hidden.
